newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Eight soldiers killed in Burundi mine blast.
newsitem.headline: Eight soldiers killed in Burundi mine blast.

text.p: Eight soldiers and four civilians were killed in a landmine explosion in Burundi, an army spokesman said on Friday.

Three soldiers including an officer and three civilians were also wounded in the blast which took place at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Thursday in Gihanga commune, Bybanza province, some 20 km (12 miles) north of the capital.
"There were eight soldiers killed because they were with the civilians in a pick-up that rolled over an anti-tank mine," army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi said. He gave no other details.

More than 150,000 people, mostly civilians, have died in Burundi's civil war since October 1993, when the country's first freely-elected Hutu president Melchior Ndadaye was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.

The war pits Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army against the armed wing of the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy. Military leader Pierre Buyoya announced a pre-ceasefire agreement last month with CNDD.
